global_issues.title: US-China chip export licensing now case-by-case +25% tariff
global_issues.note: Confirmed. BIS revised policy effective January 15, 2026 applies case-by-case review for H200, MI325X and comparable chips destined for China. 25% Section 232 tariff implemented January 14, 2026. June 2026 update extended restrictions to subsidiaries of Chinese companies headquartered outside China. Briefing claim is current and accurate.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's most serious failure is the Strait of Hormuz assessment, which is factually inverted — describing an active conflict zone with a tanker attack and US military strikes as 'stable with no new incidents' is a material error that could mislead energy sector positioning. The Google antitrust framing is months stale (the case is in appeals, not final arguments). The chip export controls are accurately described. Two critical events are absent: the June jobs miss (57k vs 110-115k) which reshapes the macro outlook, and the fact that US markets are closed today (July 3) making all watchlist actions moot until Monday July 6. Individual stock prices are broadly accurate. Do not act on the Hormuz narrative or the Google legal framing without updated sourcing.
